key_insight: A quantics tensor-train (QTT) Chebyshev–Galerkin method solves mechanics boundary-value problems directly in compressed form while preserving their variational structure.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables high-accuracy elasticity analysis across large design and uncertainty spaces without solving each configuration separately.
method: Assemble global Chebyshev–Galerkin systems in QTT form without constructing full arrays.
Handle variable coefficients, smooth geometry mappings, and mixed Dirichlet–Robin conditions.
Treat design parameters and random inputs as additional coordinates in a single compressed solve.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports errors below 10⁻⁸ on a 3D elasticity benchmark, 1.7×10⁷ cantilever designs solved in 92 s, and 2.4×10⁶-fold memory reduction versus a full coefficient array for a ten-random-coordinate problem.
watch_item: Computational gains depend on QTT compressibility; performance for less-compressible fields or nonsmooth geometries is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: A Tensor-Network Chebyshev-Galerkin Method for Boundary-Value Problems in Computational Mechanics
